cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.description:
(Findindgs assisted by Claude)

Extends #77 and #104, which showed probing and a denied worksheet read against AIHW's public Tableau server (vizprod.aihw.gov.au). This urlquery.net scan (report 3bad0896-3ef4-4b2a-afd6-5e10c667c530, 2026-06-21 03:46 UTC, scanning IP 52.202.201.157 / AS14618 Amazon) captured a URL of the form httpbin.org/base64/<payload> — httpbin's /base64/ endpoint decodes and serves whatever's in the path, so the URL itself smuggles an executable HTML+JS page.

Decoded, the script: (1) defines a helper that POSTs arbitrary strings to https://ntfy.sh/aind3b34110f4104ad7, a public pub/sub topic anyone can subscribe to; (2) calls AIHW's Tableau backend directly — startSession then bootstrapSession for workbook 'PBSdashboardallATC1-ATC2medicines-Agegroup' — bypassing the normal dashboard UI/export path; (3) parses the returned session payload, gzip-compresses it client-side via CompressionStream, base64-encodes the result, and streams it out in 3000-character chunks over the ntfy.sh channel (tagged PAGE, SID, BOOT, PART, ZIP, numbered chunks, DONE).

Unverified: whether the ntfy.sh POSTs were actually received (the scan captured the outbound script, not confirmation), and AI-company attribution.
data.summary: New AIHW exfil evidence: a June 21 03:46 UTC urlquery scan of an httpbin.org/base64-smuggled script shows a full Tableau bootstrapSession pull of AIHW's PBS dashboard, gzip+base64'd and exfiltrated in chunks via ntfy.sh POSTs
